The game feels kinda slow. One round takes around 20 minutes to complete. Could be fine, but the start is just 2 slow for my taste. Especially the starter gun makes you feel so slow. Getting the rolling item drop feels good, but completely overpowered to all other abilities, so I started not caring about slowing myself down with gun shooting and just rushed from 1 item drop to the next. Giving objectives is a great idea, but not at the cost of making certain abilities feel bad. Then I died, because I got stuck in environment without realizing, thanks to the camera occluding objects around the player. This is happening in the first level which should be the most polished. A bad omen for future levels. The builds / unlockables look super fun, but there is like 5 worlds with 5 subworlds?! and I only beat 1 level in 90 minutes (died twice in world 2). The resources I got and upgrades I bought don't feel very noticeable except for getting another class / ultimate ability. If you like grinding this might satisfy you, but it's not my cup of tea.

In the current state I wouldn't recommend it - at least from a co-op perspective. the game felt quite unbalanced. We got level 10-15 and just stood there until the timer ran out, shotgunned the boss and repeated for all the worlds. The only thing that kept us going was 100% achievement. I think it has potential, especially with all the different mechanics you can interact with in the 'overworld'. but at this state I honestly feel you could get more game for your money, especially in this genre. last note would be that later stages can get quite laggy in co-op. I am aware that more games have this issue, but this felt a bit too much. (it did get somewhat better after a performance update early December).

It commits one of the worst sins a game can: It isn't fun. The core gameplay loop feels slow, clunky, unrewarding, and frustrating. "Oh, keep playing, it gets better once you unlock more things!" No. If the game needs 10 hours and multiple unlocks to start to get engaging, I have better uses for my time. It looks very pretty, it looks like it has a large and in depth unlock system, there's all sorts of bells and whistles. But it isn't fun to play. There's no feeling of growing more powerful in a run. There's some really neat abilities that should feel powerful and good to use, but the cooldown times are atrocious, and the actual effect is rather meh at best. For a bullet heaven it misses all the marks, for a VS style game it misses all the marks, and I don't even think it works that well as an arcade SHMUP. I can't get a refund because I bought it as part of a bundle with Rogue Genesia, a game I recommend much more than this.

《Entropy Survivors》一看就是那种小成本独立游戏，画面和UI都挺廉价的，不过玩起来确实有趣，而且内容丰富，流派非常多，感觉在类幸存者这个领域也能排到T2这个级别。不过缺点就是有点肝，因为技能要升级、武器可以强化、战斗中升级刷出来的技能也可以强化，再加上本作采用的是双主角一起行动的模板，小青蛙和机器人的武器和技能我们都要强化，所以比一般的类幸存者游戏肝很多，至少我现在有的技能点到20多级还没有提示满级，不知道极限在哪里。 游戏的玩法很有趣，我们操控的主角是两位一体的，小青蛙趴在机器人身上，鼠标左键是机器人攻击，鼠标右键是小青蛙攻击，可以开自动攻击，我们只需要通过右键来调整两个人的攻击节奏就好。最主要的是角色切换之后才能释放对应的技能，换句话说机器人的技能是默认自动全开的，只要冷却好就会自动释放；但小青蛙这边我们需要按下鼠标右键才能自动释放它这边的技能。 游戏内获取技能升级方式很多，一个是升级后随机技能三选一，另一个是击败精英怪可以获得升级的箱子，箱子也会有三种情况，分别是升级1个技能、3个技能、5个技能，所以技能被堆到高等级还是很常见的。一般来说，只要有两到三个技能成型击败基本就可以碾压BOSS了。但是技能也有所区别，有些技能强度不高，点起来也没太大用，有些技能则是全屏式的清怪，基本能力就很强，升级之后释放一堆就更厉害了。 所以游戏最大的爽点是找自己合适的武器，然后搭配起来搞一套技能，技能可以用游戏里获得的宝石来提高出现的概率，相当于变相硬锁了。前期会有点折磨，因为不熟悉各种技能的效果，需要十局左右来把各个技能体验一遍，之后就知道哪个是坑哪个是神了，比如火球那个技能，一个是穿透效果，另一个每攻击到一个敌人会变大，对于这种敌人满地跑的类幸存者是最适合的，而且没升级都有一个新火球，此外还有强化燃烧伤害的技能和天赋，可以很轻松做到清屏。还有个宇宙巴掌也很牛，点气来基本没冷却，还能打断敌人攻击，基本很难有被围困的情况。 总体来说，只要你能接受那基本没有设计的UI界面和有点难受的开荒期，那么后续玩起来很快就能感受到游戏的爽点，而且双角色操纵还蛮有意思的，小鱼还是挺推荐的。

7/10 Light Recommendation. I think this game is a strong enough start. It does a lot of things right and progression feels good for a while. Around the 8+ hour mark you largely max out a couple of weapons and a mech which leaves you getting the main progression currency and the skills progression currency. The games MAIN problem that keeps me from moving forward is the limited levels you gain the skills currency on and how few of them you get from farming said levels where they do drop. I strongly believe this currency should drop from every mission generously because engaging with skills progression is FUN its just hidden behind far too much of a negative grind. The game is fun though. I got this as part of a humble bundle and it exceeded what I would have expected for a B-tier auto shooter.

It was a positive experience but there were a few caveats: - I didn't like that there are so many different gems required to grind. It made sense later but it just means more mindless grinding for no real reason. - Gameplay also felt very slow in the beginning. It got progressively better with each lot of skill tree upgrades. - I didn't like the progression went 1.1 --> 2.1 --> 3.1 --> 4.1, etc instead of 1.1 --> 1.2 --> 1.3 --> 1.4, etc. I understood why it was done like that but so we could go through each planet before going to the next rung of difficulty but It took us a hot second to figure out why the game got so hard so quickly when we went 1.1 --> 1.2 --> 1.3, etc. - Once you got used to the roster of abilities to unlock in-game, every build made you hang out for the same 10 or so weapons that were extremely useful, another 10 that were OK and the rest were either mediocre, distracting or terrible filler. So if you got a bad run of luck with what was on offer with the 3 choices, it meant the run was harder because there was no reroll. The balance was way off. There were two abilties that felt like the devs KNEW they were a bad by tying unlocking of weapons to the use of two abilites. - The pistol was better than any other weapon but A LONG SHOT. Not even close. It's a boring weapon so I didn't stick with it but my friend who I was playing co-op with did and every game would do millions of points more damage than I did just because he used the pistol. And I had upgraded the weapons to max (with 3 perks attached) and the skill tree to the same level as each other. Could not figure out why such a huge discrepancy or why any one would bother with another weapon. Pro tip: some weapons don't do a whole lot of damage but instead focus on crowd control which, later on in the game, becomes equally essential as high damage weapons. - The system that used gems to sway the likelihood of abilities showing up in-game was great in theory and a really unique way to avoid doing a reroll which I appreciated at least on paper, but I had spent lot of gems and didn't feel that was accurately reflected. I had spent gems for it to never turn up only for it turn up as often as things I spent gems on to turn as often as possible. How much gold do I need to spend on luck for that to be accurately reflected? With all that being said, there was enough to continually unlock and test which made me want to come back and continue playing. Destroying huge waves of enemies was satisfying. One small thing I loved: the upgrade for pickup radius was generously reflected in the game. It meant upgrading that skill was worth spending the gold. The levels were varied enough and each class played differently; there was plenty to like about this game. I played this co-op with a friend and we didn't experience any kind of connection issue. I can't really comment on the single player experience as I only had one run by myself and felt like it was a much better co-op experience.

The button does nothing. So the game is impossible to finish because the devs wanted to squeeze a couple more pennies out of their audience by jumping on the co-op bandwagon for a game that really doesn't need it.

I think this is a fine take on the survivors genre. In addition to the standard metaprogression upgrades you can also upgrade skills and weapons. The developers have split paying for these upgrades across multiple currencies which is initially confusing but once you know what currency is used for what upgrade it's fine. The game has multiple classes and you also have the ability to unlock alternate melee and ranged weapons. I found the performance to be pretty good, even with a lot on the screen. The visual art style isn't bad, but there is something about it that is straining to the eyes. When playing in co-op there is a long leash between players with regards to how far you can move away from each other and the camera will eventually force the players closer together which is annoying. I don't think the gameplay has a strong enough feel or the differences between classes & weapons is strong and distinct enough to where I'd want to spend time fully upgrading anything. The game has the systems to support spending more time with the game but the gameplay itself isn't strong enough to sustain that. In spite of that, the game certainly isn't bad, it's just average.
